overview: This file documents a 1932–1933 dispute over Japanese fishing vessels registered in colonial Taiwan that entered Philippine waters for fishing, small-scale trade, and the collection of natural resources. It begins with Taiwan’s licensing, tonnage, marking, logbook, and crew-qualification regulations for vessels operating south of 21° north latitude, then follows Philippine Governor-General Theodore Roosevelt Jr.’s objection that the rule could imply an incorrect northern boundary for the Philippines, whose islands extended to approximately 21°25′ north. State, War, consular, Philippine, and Taiwan officials exchanged reports and instructions, while a confidential Philippine assessment described a decade of incursions, illicit activity, arrests, escapes, and inadequate patrol capacity. Taiwan declined to amend the latitude in the regulation but circulated a clarification that Yami and North Island belonged to the Philippines and that the regulation did not authorize fishing in foreign territorial waters.

people.name: Frank LeJ. Parker
people.role: Brigadier General and Chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs, War Department
variants: Brigadier General F. Le J. Parker

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: Chief of the State Department’s Far Eastern Division

people.name: William R. Castle Jr.
people.role: State Department official signing for the Secretary of State; Under Secretary of State

people.name: Hiratsuka
people.role: Director General of Administration in the Government-General of Taiwan

people.name: Kiyokane Kohama
people.role: Chief of the Bureau of Interior and Acting Director General of Administration, Government-General of Taiwan

subfiles.title: Ketcham reports Taiwan’s controls on fishing vessels
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.to: Theodore Roosevelt Jr., Governor-General of the Philippine Islands
subfiles.about: Reports new Taiwan regulations intended to control Japanese fishing vessels operating south of the island and reduce incursions into Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham explains new rules require licenses, minimum tonnage, hull markings, logbooks, and qualified officers for Taiwan fishing craft south of 21°N, after complaints about boats entering Philippine waters, expected to reduce violations and aid Philippine identification.

subfiles.title: War Department transmits Philippine fishing correspondence
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of War
subfiles.to: U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Philippine correspondence concerning Japanese efforts to prevent fishing boats from entering Philippine waters illegally.
subfiles.summary: War Department forwards Roosevelt's and Ketcham's reports, flagging the Philippine-boundary issue raised in Roosevelt's letter's third paragraph for State's attention.

subfiles.title: Roosevelt challenges the 21° licensing line
subfiles.from: Theodore Roosevelt Jr., Governor-General of the Philippine Islands
subfiles.to: Frank LeJ. Parker, Chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs
subfiles.about: Requests correction of Taiwan’s fishing order because the 21° line could be mistaken for the Philippines’ northern boundary.
subfiles.summary: Roosevelt argues the 1898 treaty places the Philippine boundary at 21°25'N, including Y'ami and North Island, asking Taiwan's order apply south of that line, not 21°.

subfiles.title: Enclosure copy of Ketcham report with Roosevelt’s acknowledgment
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, with appended acknowledgment from Theodore Roosevelt Jr.
subfiles.to: Theodore Roosevelt Jr.; acknowledgment to John B. Ketcham
subfiles.about: Reproduces Ketcham’s report on Taiwan’s fishing controls and appends Roosevelt’s August 26 acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure repeats Taiwan's licensing, marking, and logbook rules for fishing craft south of 21°N, linking them to incursions, illegal fishing, and friction; Roosevelt's appended acknowledgment welcomes the measures as a material contribution.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on three draft communications
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: William R. Castle Jr.
subfiles.about: Reviews draft communications concerning whether the United States should seek correction of Taiwan’s fishing order.
subfiles.summary: Memo finds three draft communications formally satisfactory but advises the Far Eastern Affairs Division make no recommendation on whether to act.

subfiles.title: Stimson informs Hurley of instructions to Taihoku
subfiles.from: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Patrick J. Hurley, Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Confirms that the American consul at Taihoku has been directed to seek recognition of the 21°25′ Philippine boundary.
subfiles.summary: Stimson acknowledges the War Department's transmittal, reporting Ketcham was instructed to raise the matter with Taiwan's government, promising further updates to Hurley.

subfiles.title: State Department informs Ambassador Grew
subfiles.from: William R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends Ambassador Grew a copy of the instruction directing the Taihoku consul to address the disputed latitude.
subfiles.summary: State encloses its Ketcham instruction on Taiwan's fishing-vessel regulation to Grew, also flagging Ketcham's earlier communication already in embassy files.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Ketcham to seek correction of Order No. 33
subfiles.from: William R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: John B. Ketcham, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: Directs Ketcham to ask Taiwan authorities discreetly to move the licensing limit from 21° to 21°25′ north.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham is instructed to informally present Philippine boundary evidence and seek correction of General Order No. 33 to apply south of that boundary.

subfiles.title: Parker transmits Roosevelt’s report on Japanese activities
subfiles.from: Frank LeJ. Parker, Chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Chief of the Far Eastern Division
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential Philippine report addressing sensational press accounts of Japanese activity and vessel incursions.
subfiles.summary: Parker supplies Hornbeck with Roosevelt’s August 15 response to questions prompted by American newspaper reports about alleged Japanese activity in the Philippines. He asks that the report be treated as information rather than as a formal request for State Department action. The document is present in duplicate.

subfiles.title: Roosevelt’s confidential report on Japanese boat incursions
subfiles.from: Theodore Roosevelt Jr., Governor-General of the Philippine Islands
subfiles.to: Frank LeJ. Parker, Chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs
subfiles.about: Assesses the frequency, purposes, and enforcement problems associated with Taiwan-registered Japanese boats entering Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: Roosevelt reports decade-long Japanese boat incursions near Batanes/Babuyan and elsewhere involving illegal fishing, trade, and resource gathering, considering full prevention impossible given rough waters and scarce patrols, while rejecting rumors of broader government involvement.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledges Parker’s confidential information
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck
subfiles.to: Frank LeJ. Parker
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Roosevelt’s report and its restriction to informational use.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says Parker's letter and Roosevelt's account interest him, noting Parker's handling request and Roosevelt's view that no immediate action was warranted.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs synopsis of Taihoku despatch No. 46
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Internal State Department circulation
subfiles.about: Summarizes Ketcham’s initial approach to Taiwan officials about the disputed latitude.
subfiles.summary: Memo explains Ketcham relayed the Philippine request to shift the boundary reference to 21°25', with Taiwan promising to examine it, possibly needing Tokyo consultation.

subfiles.title: Ketcham reports initial interview with Hiratsuka
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.to: U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports presenting the Philippine boundary request to Taiwan’s Director General of Administration.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham reports interview delays from Hiratsuka's Tokyo absence and holidays; on January 4 he described the boundary and requested amending Order No. 33, with Hiratsuka promising investigation but likely needing Tokyo approval.

subfiles.title: Stimson updates Hurley on Ketcham’s initial approach
subfiles.from: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Patrick J. Hurley, Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards despatch No. 46 and reports that Taiwan authorities are considering the Philippine boundary question.
subfiles.summary: Stimson supplements his November correspondence by enclosing Ketcham’s January 4 despatch. He notes that the facts were presented to Taiwan’s Director General of Administration, who agreed to investigate and inform the consulate of the government-general’s decision. The State Department promises further updates.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs synopsis of Taihoku despatch No. 53
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Internal State Department circulation
subfiles.about: Assesses Taiwan’s circular clarification as a practical recognition of the true Philippine boundary despite refusal to amend the order.
subfiles.summary: Memo reports Taiwan told officials 21° was a licensing limit, not the Philippine boundary, recognizing islands north of it, sufficient to correct misunderstanding.

subfiles.title: Ketcham reports negotiated clarification of Order No. 33
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.to: U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports Taiwan’s refusal to amend its fishing order and its agreement instead to warn officials that Philippine islands lay north of 21°.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham found Taiwan unwilling to concede the Philippine boundary shaped its regulation, framing it as shipwreck/dispute prevention, but secured a compromise circular naming Yami and North Island as Philippine territory and clarifying no application within foreign waters.

subfiles.title: Kohama notifies Ketcham that governors received the clarification
subfiles.from: Kiyokane Kohama, Acting Director General of Administration
subfiles.to: John B. Ketcham, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: Confirms that Taiwan’s local governors were sent a notice clarifying the fishing-control regulation.
subfiles.summary: Kohama tells Ketcham that local governors were notified of the fishing-rule clarification, enclosing a copy of the notice.

subfiles.title: Taiwan circular on motor fishing vessels and Philippine islands
subfiles.from: Kiyokane Kohama, Acting Director General of Administration
subfiles.to: Provincial governors of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Orders stronger enforcement against unlicensed vessels and clarifies that the 21° licensing line is not the Philippine boundary.
subfiles.summary: Circular says unlicensed fishing persisted, explains the 21° line prevented shipwrecks/disputes rather than defining the boundary, naming Yami/North Island as Philippine, instructing governors to publicize no application in foreign waters.

subfiles.title: Hull informs Dern of Taiwan’s boundary clarification
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: George H. Dern, Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards despatch No. 53 and explains the outcome of Ketcham’s negotiations with Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Hull tells Dern Taiwan declined to amend Order No. 33 but sent governors letters clarifying 21°N wasn't the Philippine boundary, enclosing Ketcham's despatch.

subfiles.title: War Department acknowledges the final Taiwan report
subfiles.from: George H. Dern, Secretary of War
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the State Department’s final report and transmits it to the acting Philippine governor-general.
subfiles.summary: War Department confirms receiving Hull's letter and Ketcham's final despatch, forwarding copies to the Acting Governor-General of the Philippines.

interest: Shows a Taiwan fishing-regulation dispute testing sovereignty, Philippine-boundary claims, and diplomatic compromise over licensing.
